_doc: Wire schema for sleuth_mcp tool-call return shapes. Sidecar-only — the root sleuth package does not ship a parallel copy. Audit source: packages/sleuth_mcp/test/schema/mcp_tool_schema_audit_test.dart. Human-readable render at mcp_tool_schema.md.
notes: Error envelopes describe current sidecar handler behavior — each handler returns ToolCallResult.text(...) with `isError: true` and a single text content carrying the message string. Codes listed in `errors[].code` appear verbatim as the prefix of that text. A centralized typed error class is acknowledged debt.

Passthrough tools delegate to bridge.callExtension and return the ext.sleuth.* envelope unmodified. Documented shims (get_route_health v0.32 -> v0.33 wrapper, get_issues severityAtLeast filter) are spelled out explicitly so the audit can assert the shim's behavior.
Snapshot / route-session nested shapes live in mcp_schema.{json,md}. This file documents only the tool-layer wrapping.

diskHandoff.doc: When true, write the envelope to a temp file; the tool returns {path, sizeBytes, sha256, _projectedSections?, _projectionLimits?, _projectionApplied?} instead of inline data.

shims.name: disk_handoff
shims.doc: When `diskHandoff` is true the sidecar serializes the snapshot envelope to a per-process Directory.systemTemp/sleuth_snapshot_<pid>/<random>.json file (128-bit Random.secure name). The per-pid dir is created 0700 and the file 0600, both verified via FileStat; if owner-only perms cannot be set+verified on POSIX the file is deleted and a `disk_handoff_failed` error is returned (fail-closed). On Windows POSIX modes don't apply. The payload MAY contain mildly-sensitive data (e.g. recentRequests[].url with query tokens), hence the fail-closed perms. Returns {path, sizeBytes, sha256} plus any projection metadata, rather than the inline `data` block. Files are deleted on detach_app, on sidecar shutdown, and aged files (30 min) in the process's own dir are swept on each new write (per-pid dir prevents cross-instance sweeps). When `diskHandoff` is false/absent the envelope passes through unmodified. Lineage fallback: if the app predates projection support and a projection arg was requested, the sidecar stamps `_projectionApplied: by_sidecar_fallback` on the disk-handoff path; on the inline path it returns `projection_unsupported_by_app` instead (the full payload would overflow the response cap).

shims.name: severity_filter
shims.doc: When `severityAtLeast` is `warning` or `critical`, the sidecar filters `data.issues` to entries whose severity meets the threshold AND adds `data.severityAtLeast` echoing the requested level. When `severityAtLeast` is `ok` or absent, the envelope passes through unmodified.

shims.name: lineage_route_wrapper
shims.doc: When the `route` arg is provided and the bridge is connected to an `acceptedPriorLineages` app emitting the v0.32 inline RouteSession shape (data carries `routeName` but no `route` key), the shim wraps data into `{route: <inline-session>}` so downstream consumers always see the canonical v0.33 envelope. v0.33+ apps already emit the wrapper and pass through untouched. Error envelopes and absent-route shapes are never wrapped.
